units.en: Treatise 25: Officials, Part Two.
units.literal: Treatise twenty-five: Officials, Part Two.

units.zh: 太常 光禄勋 卫尉 太仆 廷尉 大鸿胪
units.en: The Minister of Ceremonies, the Minister of the Household, the Minister of the Guard, the Minister Coachman, the Minister of Justice, and the Grand Herald.
units.literal: Minister of Ceremonies, Minister of the Household, Minister of the Guard, Minister Coachman, Minister of Justice, Grand Herald.

units.zh: 太常，卿一人，中二千石。
units.en: The Minister of Ceremonies: one minister at the top salary grade of two thousand bushels.
units.literal: Minister of Ceremonies: minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌礼仪祭祀。
units.en: He oversees court ritual, ceremonial protocol, and state sacrifices.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds rites, protocol, and sacrifices.

units.zh: 每祭祀，先奏其礼仪；
units.en: Before every sacrifice he memorializes the order of rites to be observed;
units.literal: On each sacrifice, he first presents the ritual protocol;

units.zh: 及行事，常赞天子。
units.en: during the rite itself he prompts the emperor with the liturgical responses.
units.literal: when carrying them out, he constantly assists the Son of Heaven with recitations.

units.zh: 汉旧仪曰：「赞飨一人，秩六百石，掌赞天子。」
units.en: The Old Han Ceremonies names one libation assistant at six hundred bushels to prompt the emperor during the feast."
units.literal: The Old Han Ceremonies says: "One libation assistant, rank six hundred bushels, masters assisting the Son of Heaven."

units.zh: 每选试博士，奏其能否。
units.en: Whenever erudites sit for promotion or examination, he reports on their competence.
units.literal: Whenever erudites are selected and examined, he reports whether they are qualified or not.

units.zh: 大射、养老、大丧，皆奏其礼仪。
units.en: The grand archery, the honoring of the aged, and state funerals all require his memorial on correct ritual.
units.literal: For the grand archery, elder nurturing, and great mourning, all he presents their ritual protocols.

units.zh: 每月前晦，察行陵庙。
units.en: On the eve of each month’s last day he tours the imperial tombs and ancestral shrines to see that all is in order.
units.literal: Each month on the last day before the dark moon, he inspects progress at the mausoleums and shrines.

units.zh: 丞一人，比千石。
units.en: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 六百石。
units.en: Some registers list that post at six hundred bushels instead.
units.literal: Six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌凡行礼及祭祀小事，总署曹事。
units.en: The assistant handles routine observances and minor cult matters and coordinates the ministry’s bureaus.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds general conduct of rites and small matters of sacrifice, and overall superintends bureau affairs.

units.zh: 汉旧仪曰：「丞举庙中非法者。」
units.en: The Old Han Ceremonies requires the assistant to report ritual violations in the ancestral shrine."
units.literal: The Old Han Ceremonies says: "The assistant reports unlawful conduct in the shrine."

units.zh: 其署曹掾史，随事为员，诸卿皆然。
units.en: Bureau staff numbers flex with the workload; the same rule applies across the nine ministers.
units.literal: As for the bureau attendants and clerks in his office, according to affairs they make up the quota; all the ministers are thus.

units.zh: 太史令一人，六百石。
units.en: One Director of Astronomy at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of Astronomy, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌天時、星歷。
units.en: He watches the seasons, weather patterns, stars, and the civil calendar.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds seasons and weather, stars and calendars.

units.zh: 凡歲將終，奏新年歷。
units.en: At year’s end he presents the almanac for the coming year.
units.literal: Whenever the year is about to end, he presents the calendar for the new year.

units.zh: 凡国祭祀、丧、娶之事，掌奏良日及时节禁忌。
units.en: For state sacrifices, funerals, and royal weddings he proposes lucky dates and seasonal taboos.
units.literal: For state sacrifices, mourning, and marriage matters, he presents auspicious days and timely prohibitions.

units.zh: 凡国有瑞应、灾异，掌记之。
units.en: He logs auspicious omens and ill portents for the archives.
units.literal: For state prodigies of auspicious response and disasters or anomalies, he records them.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「太史待诏三十七人，其六人治历，三人龟卜，三人庐宅，四人日时，三人易筮，二人典禳，九人籍氏、许氏、典昌氏，各三人，嘉法、请雨、解事各二人，医一人。」
units.en: The Offices of Han assigns thirty-seven awaiting-edict astronomers to calendars, divination, timing, exorcism, clan specialists, rain prayers, case work, and one court physician."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Thirty-seven awaiting-edict officers of the Director of Astronomy: six manage calendars, three turtle divination, three house-site divination, four day-and-time, three Changes divination, two exorcism, nine of the Ji, Xu, and Dianchang clans three each, auspicious methods, rain prayers, and case resolution two each, one physician."

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 明堂及灵台丞一人，二百石。
units.en: One deputy for the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace at two hundred bushels.
units.literal: Assistant for the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace, one person, two hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：二丞，掌守明堂、灵台。
units.en: Commentary: paired deputies keep watch over the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace.
units.literal: Original commentary: the two assistants guard the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace.

units.zh: 灵台掌候日月星气，皆属太史。
units.en: The Spiritual Terrace tracks sun, moon, stars, and ether—all under the Director of Astronomy.
units.literal: The Spiritual Terrace masters observing sun, moon, stars, and vapors; all belong to the Director of Astronomy.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「灵台待诏四十一人，其十四人候星，二人候日，三人候风，十二人候气，三人候晷景，七人候钟律。
units.en: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one Spiritual Terrace awaiting-edict officers: fourteen for stars, two for the sun, three for wind, twelve for vapors, three for sundials, seven for pitch pipes,
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one awaiting-edict officers at the Spiritual Terrace: fourteen observe stars, two observe the sun, three observe wind, twelve observe vapors, three observe gnomon shadows, seven observe pitch pipes and measures.

units.zh: 一人舍人。」
units.en: and one attendant."
units.literal: One attendant."

units.zh: 博士祭酒一人，六百石。
units.en: One erudite libationer at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Erudite libationer, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本仆射，中兴转为祭酒。
units.en: The head of the erudites was originally titled Pushe; after the restoration the office was renamed libationer (jijiu).
units.literal: Originally Erudite Pushe; at restoration changed to libationer.

units.zh: 胡广曰：「官名祭酒，皆一位之元长者也。
units.en: Hu Guang explained: "The title jijiu marks the senior head of a bureau.
units.literal: Hu Guang said: "The office title libationer designates the senior head of a single rank.

units.zh: 古礼，宾客得主人馔，则老者一人举酒以祭于地，旧说以为示有先。」
units.en: In ancient guest ritual the eldest would pour a libation to the ground to honor those who came before."
units.literal: In ancient ritual, when guests received food from the host, the eldest among them would raise wine and offer it to the ground; older explanations hold that this showed regard for ancestors."

units.zh: 博士十四人，比六百石。
units.en: Fourteen court erudites at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Fourteen erudites, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：《易》四，施、孟、梁丘、京氏。
units.en: The Book of Changes is taught in four schools—Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing.
units.literal: Original commentary: for the Changes, four traditions: Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing.

units.zh: 《尚书》三，欧阳、大小夏侯氏。
units.en: The Book of Documents has three lines—Ouyang and the elder and younger Xiahou traditions.
units.literal: For the Documents, three: Ouyang, Greater and Lesser Xiahou.

units.zh: 《诗》三，鲁、齐、韩氏。
units.en: The Odes are represented by the Lu, Qi, and Han schools.
units.literal: For the Odes, three: Lu, Qi, and Han.

units.zh: 《礼》二，大小戴氏。
units.en: The Rites survive in the elder and younger Dai recensions.
units.literal: For the Rites, two: Greater and Lesser Dai.

units.zh: 《春秋》二，《公羊》严、颜氏。
units.en: The Spring and Autumn is taught in two Gongyang schools, the lineages of Master Yan Pengzu and Master Yan Anle.
units.literal: For the Spring and Autumn, two: the Gongyang traditions of Yan and Yan.

units.zh: 掌教弟子。
units.en: They instruct the disciples enrolled at the academy.
units.literal: They master teaching disciples.

units.zh: 國有疑事，掌承問對。
units.en: When policy questions arise, they supply learned answers on demand.
units.literal: When the state has doubtful matters, they undertake to answer inquiries.

units.zh: 本四百石，宣帝增秩。
units.en: Their stipend began at four hundred bushels until Emperor Xuan raised it.
units.literal: Originally four hundred bushels; Emperor Xuan increased the rank.

units.zh: 太祝令一人，六百石。
units.en: One Director of Invocations at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of Invocations, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：凡国祭祀，掌读祝及迎送神。
units.en: At state sacrifices he chants the prayer texts and conducts the spirits’ arrival and departure.
units.literal: Original commentary: for state sacrifices, he reads invocations and welcomes and sends off the spirits.

units.zh: 汉旧仪曰：「庙祭，太祝令主席酒。」
units.en: The Old Han Ceremonies makes the Director of Invocations preside over the libation at ancestral rites."
units.literal: The Old Han Ceremonies says: "At shrine sacrifice, the Director of Invocations presides over the libation wine."

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏四十一人，其二人百石，二人斗食，二十二人佐，二人学事，四人守学事，九人有秩。
units.en: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one clerks
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one staff: two at one hundred bushels, two at dou-food rank, twenty-two assistants, two student clerks, four supervising student clerks, nine with stipends.

units.zh: 百五十人祝人，宰二百四十二人，屠者六十人。」
units.en: plus 150 invokers, 242 butchers, and 60 slaughterers for the shrine staff."
units.literal: One hundred fifty invokers, two hundred forty-two butchers, sixty slaughterers."

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌祝小神事。
units.en: The assistant tends invocations to secondary cults.
units.literal: Original commentary: he masters invocation of lesser deity affairs.

units.zh: 太宰令一人，六百石。
units.en: One Director of the Grand Butcher at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of the Grand Butcher, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌宰工鼎俎馔具之物。
units.en: He supervised butchers, vessels, and sacrificial food preparations.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds butcher-craftsmen, tripods, meat stands, and prepared offerings.

units.zh: 凡国祭祀，掌陈馔具。
units.en: At state sacrifices he arranged the food offerings.
units.literal: For state sacrifices, he masters arranging prepared offerings.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「明堂丞一人，二百石。
units.en: The Offices of Han says: "The Bright Hall has one two-hundred-bushel assistant,
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "One Bright Hall assistant at two hundred bushels.

units.zh: 员吏四十二人，其二人百石，二人斗食，二十三人佐，九人有秩，二人学事，四人守学事。
units.en: forty-two clerks,
units.literal: Forty-two staff: two at one hundred bushels, two at dou-food rank, twenty-three assistants, nine with stipends, two student clerks, four supervising student clerks.

units.zh: 宰二百四十二人，屠者七十三人，卫士一十五人。」
units.en: 242 butchers, 73 slaughterers, and 15 guards."
units.literal: Two hundred forty-two butchers, seventy-three slaughterers, fifteen guards."

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 大予乐令一人，本注曰：掌伎乐。
units.en: One Director of Grand Imperial Music, charged with court performance and ritual music.
units.literal: Director of the Grand Imperial Music, one person; original commentary: he holds performances and music.

units.zh: 凡国祭祀，掌请奏乐，及大飨用乐，掌其陈序。
units.en: He schedules music at sacrifices and arranges the program for great banquets that include orchestral performance.
units.literal: For state sacrifices, he requests and presents music; for great feasts using music, he holds their arrangement and order.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 高庙令一人，六百石。
units.en: One keeper of Emperor Gaozu’s shrine at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Gaozu’s shrine director, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：守庙，掌案行扫除。
units.en: He tends the shrine, inspects its precincts, and keeps them swept.
units.literal: Original commentary: guards the shrine; masters inspection tours and sweeping.

units.zh: 无丞。
units.en: There is no deputy to this office.
units.literal: No assistant.

units.zh: 世祖庙令一人，六百石。
units.en: One keeper of Guangwu’s shrine at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Founding Ancestor’s shrine director, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：如高庙。
units.en: His duties mirror those at Gaozu’s shrine.
units.literal: Original commentary: as for Gaozu’s shrine.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏六人，卫士二十人。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists six clerks and twenty guards."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Six staff and twenty guards."

units.zh: 先帝陵，每陵园令各一人，六百石。
units.en: Each deceased emperor's mausoleum park had one director at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: For former emperors' mausoleums, each mausoleum park has one director, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌守陵园，案行扫除。
units.en: He keeps the mausoleum grounds and inspects sweeping and upkeep.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds guarding the mausoleum park and inspects sweeping and cleaning.

units.zh: 丞及校长各一人。
units.en: Each park has one assistant and one camp commandant.
units.literal: One assistant and one commandant each.

units.zh: 本注曰：校长，主兵戎盗贼事。
units.en: The commandant handles armed watch and suppresses banditry within the park.
units.literal: Original commentary: the commandant masters weapons, troops, bandits, and thieves.

units.zh: 先帝陵，每陵食官令各一人，六百石。
units.en: Each imperial tomb also has a granary director at six hundred bushels for offerings.
units.literal: For former emperors’ mausoleums, each mausoleum has one granary director, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌望晦时节祭祀。
units.en: He presides over the monthly offering rites at the new and dark moons.
units.literal: Original commentary: masters new-moon and dark-moon seasonal sacrifices.

units.zh: 右属太常。
units.en: The offices listed at right fall under the Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 本注曰：有祠祀令一人，后转属少府。
units.en: There used to be a director of shrine offerings; that post was later moved to the Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
units.literal: Original commentary: there was one director of shrine offerings, later transferred to the Minister of the Lesser Treasury.

units.zh: 有太卜令，六百石，后省并太史。
units.en: The old Director of Grand Divination at six hundred bushels was cut and folded into the Director of Astronomy.
units.literal: There was a director of grand divination, six hundred bushels; later abolished and merged into the Director of Astronomy.

units.zh: 中兴以来，省前凡十官。
units.en: Since the Eastern restoration, ten Western Han offices in this ministry have been abolished.
units.literal: Since the restoration, ten offices in all from before were eliminated.

units.zh: 案前书，十官者，太宰、均官、都水、雍太祝、五畤各一尉也。
units.en: The Former Book lists ten offices—Grand Butcher, Equalization, Capital Waters, Yong Grand Invocator, and the Five Altars—each with its own commandant.
units.literal: According to the Former Book, the ten offices were: Grand Butcher, Equalization, Capital Waters, Yong Grand Invocator, and Five Altars—each with one commandant.

units.zh: 东观书曰：「章帝又置祀令、丞，延平元年省。」
units.en: The Eastern Lodge Record notes that Emperor Zhang added sacrifice directors, cut in Yanping 1."
units.literal: The Eastern Lodge Record says: "Emperor Zhang also set up directors and assistants of sacrifices; they were abolished in the first year of Yanping."

units.zh: 光禄勋，卿一人，中二千石。
units.en: The Minister of the Household: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
units.literal: Minister of the Household, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌宿卫宫殿门户，典谒署郎更直执戟，宿卫门户，考其德行而进退之。
units.en: He commands palace gate security, runs the audience bureaus, and rotates gentlemen-of-the-house on halberd watch while judging their conduct for promotion or dismissal.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds night-watch at palace gates and doors, manages reception offices and gentlemen-of-the-house in rotating watch bearing halberds, night-watch at gates and doors, examines their conduct and virtue and promotes or demotes them.

units.zh: 胡广曰：「勋犹门昏也，易曰『为门昏寺』。
units.en: Hu Guang derived xun from gate-warding, citing the Changes line on gate temples;
units.literal: Hu Guang said: "Xun means gate-ward, as the Changes says 'he made gate-ward temples.

units.zh: 宦寺，主殿宫门户之职。」
units.en: the palace eunuch bureaus guarded the palace gates."
units.literal: Eunuch temples master the duty of palace gates and doors."

units.zh: 郊祀之事，掌三献。
units.en: At suburban sacrifices he presents the three ritual libations of wine.
units.literal: In suburban sacrifice affairs, he presents the three libations.

units.zh: 丞一人，比千石。
units.en: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 五官中郎将一人，比二千石。
units.en: One captain of the central gentlemen for the five bureaus at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the five offices, one person, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主五官郎。
units.en: He leads the gentlemen attached to the five ministries.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands the gentlemen for the five offices.

units.zh: 五官中郎，比六百石。
units.en: Central gentlemen for the five bureaus at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen of the house for the five offices at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 胡广曰：「光禄大夫，本为中大夫，武帝元狩五年置谏大夫为光禄大夫，世祖中兴，以为谏议大夫。
units.en: Hu Guang said: "The Household Grandee was originally the Middle Grandee; in the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu remonstrating grandees were made household grandees, and at Guangwu's restoration they became remonstrating grandees.
units.literal: Hu Guang said: "The Household Grandee was originally Middle Grandee. In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu remonstrating grandees were made household grandees; at Emperor Guangwu's restoration they became remonstrating grandees.

units.zh: 又有太中、中散大夫。
units.en: alongside palace and scattered grandees
units.literal: There were also grandees within the palace and grandees of scattered attendance.

units.zh: 此四等于古皆为天子之下大夫，视列国之上卿。」
units.en: —four grades matching the ancient lower grandees of the ruler."
units.literal: These four grades in antiquity were all the Son of Heaven's lower grandees, equivalent to the upper ministers of feudal states."

units.zh: 汉官曰三十人。
units.en: The Offices of Han sets the quota at thirty.
units.literal: The Offices of Han says thirty men.

units.zh: 郎年五十以屬五官，故曰六百石。
units.en: Gentlemen aged fifty were attached to the Five Offices, so they were said to be six hundred shi.
units.literal: Gentlemen aged fifty were attached to the Five Offices, so they were said to be six hundred shi.

units.zh: 五官侍郎，比四百石。
units.en: Attendant gentlemen for the five bureaus at four hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen attendants for the five offices, comparable to four hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：無員。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 五官郎中，比三百石。
units.en: Secretary gentlemen for the five bureaus at three hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen secretaries for the five offices, comparable to three hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 凡郎官皆主更直执戟，宿卫诸殿门，出充车骑。
units.en: Gentlemen-of-the-house stand rotating halberd watch at palace doors and ride out as imperial escort.
units.literal: All gentlemen-of-the-house chiefly rotate watch bearing halberds, night-watch at the various hall gates, and go out to act as chariots and cavalry escort.

units.zh: 唯议郎不在直中。
units.en: Advisory gentlemen alone are exempt from guard duty.
units.literal: Only advisory gentlemen are not in the watch rotation.

units.zh: 左中郎将，比二千石。
units.en: The left captain of the central gentlemen at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Left leader of gentlemen-of-the-house at middle rank, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主左署郎。
units.en: He commands gentlemen of the left wing.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands gentlemen of the left bureau.

units.zh: 中郎，比六百石。
units.en: Central gentlemen at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 侍郎，比四百石。
units.en: Attendant gentlemen at four hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen attendants, comparable to four hundred bushels.

units.zh: 郎中，比三百石。
units.en: Secretary gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.

units.zh: 三郎。
units.en: Three gentlemen.
units.literal: Three gentlemen.

units.zh: 本注曰：皆无员。
units.en: Again, no statutory quotas.
units.literal: Original commentary: all have no fixed quota.

units.zh: 右中郎將，比二千石。
units.en: The right captain of the central gentlemen at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Right leader of gentlemen-of-the-house at middle rank, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主右署郎。
units.en: He commands gentlemen of the right wing.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands gentlemen of the right bureau.

units.zh: 中郎，比六百石。
units.en: Central gentlemen at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 侍郎，比四百石。
units.en: Attendant gentlemen at four hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen attendants, comparable to four hundred bushels.

units.zh: 郎中，比三百石。
units.en: Secretary gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：皆无员。
units.en: Again, no statutory quotas.
units.literal: Original commentary: all have no fixed quota.

units.zh: 三郎，并无员。
units.en: All three gentleman corps lacked fixed quotas.
units.literal: The three corps of gentlemen all have no fixed quota.

units.zh: 虎贲中郎将，比二千石。
units.en: The captain of the household rapid guard at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the tiger-rank bodyguard, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主虎贲宿衛。
units.en: He leads the rapid guards who stand night watch at close quarters.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands tiger-rank bodyguard night-watch.

units.zh: 前书武帝置期门，平帝更名虎贲。
units.en: The Former Book records that Emperor Wu created the Gate of Expected Arrival and Emperor Ping renamed it the rapid guard.
units.literal: The Former Book says Emperor Wu set up the Gate of Expected Arrival; Emperor Ping renamed it Tiger-Rank Guard.

units.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「主虎贲千五百人，无常员，多至千人。
units.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "They command 1,500 rapid guards, without a fixed quota, often up to a thousand.
units.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "They command one thousand five hundred tiger-rank guards, no fixed quota, often up to one thousand.

units.zh: 戴鹖冠，次右将府。」
units.en: wearing pheasant caps and quartered next to the right general's office."
units.literal: They wear pheasant caps and rank next to the right general's bureau."

units.zh: 又虎贲旧作「虎奔」，言如虎之奔也，王莽以古有勇士孟贲，故名焉。
units.en: The name was once written "tiger-run" for swiftness; Wang Mang linked it to the ancient warrior Meng Ben.
units.literal: Formerly hu-ben was written "tiger-run," meaning to run like a tiger; Wang Mang, because antiquity had the warrior Meng Ben, therefore gave the name.

units.zh: 孔安国曰「若虎贲兽」，言其甚猛。
units.en: Kong Anguo said they were "like tiger-rank beasts," meaning they were very fierce.
units.literal: Kong Anguo said "like the tiger-rank beast," meaning they are very fierce.

units.zh: 左右仆射、左右陛长各一人，比六百石。
units.en: Left and right adjutants and left and right stair captains—one of each at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Left and right shooting supervisors and left and right stairhead captains, one each, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：仆射，主虎贲郎习射。
units.en: The adjutants drill the rapid guard in archery.
units.literal: Original commentary: shooting supervisors command tiger-rank gentlemen in archery practice.

units.zh: 陛长，主直虎贲，朝会在殿中。
units.en: Stair captains post rapid guards inside the hall during audiences.
units.literal: Stairhead captains command watch-standing tiger-rank guards; at court assemblies they are in the hall.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「陛长，墨绶铜印。」
units.en: The Offices of Han gives stair captains black ribbons and bronze seals."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Stairhead captains, black ribbon and bronze seal."

units.zh: 虎贲中郎，比六百石。
units.en: Rapid-guard central gentlemen at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Tiger-rank gentlemen at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 虎贲侍郎，比四百石。
units.en: Rapid-guard attendant gentlemen at four hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Tiger-rank gentlemen attendants, comparable to four hundred bushels.

units.zh: 虎贲郎中，比三百石。
units.en: Rapid-guard secretary gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Tiger-rank gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.

units.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「虎贲诸郎，皆父死子代，汉制也。」
units.en: Xun Chuo noted that rapid-guard gentlemen inherited from father to son under Han rule."
units.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "All tiger-rank gentlemen succeed father to son; this is Han institution."

units.zh: 节从虎贲，比二百石。
units.en: Halberd-bearing rapid guards at two hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Halberd-following tiger-rank guards, comparable to two hundred bushels.

units.zh: 四郎。
units.en: Four gentleman corps.
units.literal: Four corps of gentlemen.

units.zh: 本注曰：皆无员。
units.en: Again, no statutory quotas.
units.literal: Original commentary: all have no fixed quota.

units.zh: 掌宿卫侍从。
units.en: They provide close escort and night security for the throne.
units.literal: They hold night-watch attendance and following.

units.zh: 自节从虎贲久者转迁，才能差高至中郎。
units.en: Veterans of the halberd-bearing guard rotate upward, and the abler among them may rise to central gentleman.
units.literal: From halberd-following tiger-rank guards, those long in service transfer and advance; according to ability, somewhat higher reach middle gentlemen rank.

units.zh: 羽林中郎将，比二千石。
units.en: The captain of the Feathered Forest guard at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the feathered forest, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主羽林郎。
units.en: He commands the Feathered Forest gentlemen.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands feathered-forest gentlemen.

units.zh: 羽林郎，比三百石。
units.en: Feathered Forest gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Feathered-forest gentlemen, comparable to three hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 掌宿卫侍从。
units.en: They provide close escort and night security for the throne.
units.literal: They hold night-watch attendance and following.

units.zh: 常选汉阳、陇西、安定、北地、上郡、西河凡六郡良家补。
units.en: Recruits are drawn in rotation from respectable households across six northwestern commanderies.
units.literal: They are regularly selected from the six commanderies Hanyang, Longxi, Anding, Beidi, Shangjun, and Xihe, good families to fill the ranks.

units.zh: 本武帝以便马从猎，还宿殿陛巖下室中，故号巖郎。
units.en: Emperor Wu first rode light mounts on the hunt and billeted his escort under the hall steps, whence the nickname “gallery guard.”
units.literal: Originally Emperor Wu used nimble mounts to follow the hunt, returning to lodge in the chamber beneath the palace steps, therefore they were called “step-gentlemen.”

units.zh: 前书曰初置名建章营骑，后更名。
units.en: The Former Book records that the corps was first titled Jianzhang camp cavalry and later renamed.
units.literal: The Former Book says at first they were set up as Jianzhang camp cavalry, later renamed.

units.zh: 出补三百石丞、尉。
units.en: Veterans were posted out as three-hundred-bushel assistants and commandants.
units.literal: On leaving service they are supplemented as three-hundred-bushel assistants and commandants.

units.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「言其严厉整锐也。」
units.en: Xun Chuo glossed the name as denoting stern discipline and sharp readiness."
units.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "This means stern, severe, and sharp."

units.zh: 案此则为岩郎，与志不同。
units.en: This account treats them as gallery guards, which differs from the treatise elsewhere.
units.literal: On investigation this refers to gallery gentlemen, differing from the treatise.

units.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「羽林郎百二十八人，无常员，府次虎贲府。」
units.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "128 Feathered Forest gentlemen without a fixed quota, quartered next to the rapid guard."
units.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "One hundred twenty-eight Feathered Forest gentlemen, no fixed quota; the bureau ranks next to the Tiger-Rank Guard bureau."

units.zh: 羽林左监一人，六百石。
units.en: One left superintendent of the Feathered Forest at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Left superintendent of the Feathered Forest, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主羽林左骑。
units.en: He commands the left wing of Feathered Forest cavalry.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands the Feathered Forest left cavalry.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 羽林右监一人，六百石。
units.en: One right superintendent of the Feathered Forest at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Right superintendent of the Feathered Forest, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主羽林右骑。
units.en: He commands the right wing of Feathered Forest cavalry.
units.literal: Original commentary: he commands the Feathered Forest right cavalry.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 奉车都尉，比二千石。
units.en: Commandants of the imperial chariot at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Commandant of the imperial chariot, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 掌御乘舆车。
units.en: They drive and maintain the emperor’s traveling carriages.
units.literal: He holds the imperial carriage and chariots.

units.zh: 驸马都尉，比二千石。
units.en: Commandants of the horse escort at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Commandant of the horse escort, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 汉官曰五人。
units.en: The Offices of Han sets the quota at five.
units.literal: The Offices of Han says five men.

units.zh: 掌驸马。
units.en: He commands the emperor's horse escort.
units.literal: He holds the horse escort.

units.zh: 骑都尉，比二千石。
units.en: Commandants of cavalry at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Commandant of cavalry, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 本监羽林骑。
units.en: The post originally oversaw Feathered Forest mounted troops.
units.literal: Originally they supervised Feathered Forest cavalry.

units.zh: 光禄大夫，比二千石。
units.en: Household grandees at two thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Household grandee, comparable to two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 凡大夫、议郎皆掌顾问应对，无常事，唯诏令所使。
units.en: Household grandees and advisory gentlemen serve as ad hoc consultants, with no standing portfolio beyond what an edict assigns.
units.literal: As for grandees and advisory gentlemen, all hold counsel and response; there are no constant duties; only as edicts and orders dispatch them.

units.zh: 凡诸国嗣之丧，则光禄大夫掌吊。
units.en: When a feudal heir dies, a household grandee leads the court’s mission of condolence.
units.literal: Whenever feudal states’ heirs die, then the household grandee masters condolence missions.

units.zh: 太中大夫，千石。
units.en: Grandees within the palace at one thousand bushels.
units.literal: Grandee within the palace, one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 中散大夫，六百石。
units.en: Grandees of scattered attendance at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Grandee of scattered attendance, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 谏议大夫，六百石。
units.en: Remonstrating grandees at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Grandee remonstrant, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：无员。
units.en: There is no statutory head count.
units.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 议郎，六百石，本注曰：无员。
units.en: Advisory gentlemen at six hundred bushels, without a statutory quota.
units.literal: Advisory gentleman, six hundred bushels; original commentary: no fixed quota.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「五十人，无常员。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists fifty men without a fixed quota."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Fifty men, no fixed quota."

units.zh: 谒者仆射一人，比千石。
units.en: One chief receptionist at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Shepherd of receptionists, one person, comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：为谒者台率，主谒者，天子出，奉引。
units.en: He heads the reception corps, and when the emperor leaves the palace he leads the vanguard.
units.literal: Original commentary: he is leader of the receptionists' bureau, commands receptionists; when the Son of Heaven goes out, he leads the procession.

units.zh: 古重习武，有主射以督录之。
units.en: Antiquity prized martial drill; a master archer supervised the corps.
units.literal: In antiquity they valued martial practice; there was a master of archery to supervise and record them.

units.zh: 故曰仆射。
units.en: Hence the title pushe, "shepherd of archers."
units.literal: Therefore it is called "shepherd" (pushe).

units.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「见尚书令，对揖无敬。
units.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "When they meet the Master of Writing, they exchange bows without full prostration,
units.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "When meeting the Master of Writing, they bow facing each other without full obeisance.

units.zh: 谒者见，执板拜之。」
units.en: but bowed with tablets to receptionists."
units.literal: When receptionists meet, they hold the tablet and bow."

units.zh: 常侍谒者五人，比六百石。
units.en: Five standing receptionists at six hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Constant attendant receptionists, five persons, comparable to six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主殿上时节威仪。
units.en: They regulate ritual pacing and demeanor during audiences.
units.literal: Original commentary: they hold seasonal order and ceremony on the hall above.

units.zh: 谒者三十人。
units.en: Thirty receptionists serve in rotation.
units.literal: Thirty receptionists.

units.zh: 其给事谒者，四百石。
units.en: Serving receptionists draw four hundred bushels.
units.literal: Those who are serving receptionists, four hundred bushels.

units.zh: 其灌谒者郎中，比三百石。
units.en: Bathed receptionists acting as gentleman secretaries rank at three hundred bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Those who are bathed receptionists and gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌宾赞受事，及上章报问。
units.en: They greet envoys, take in petitions, and carry answers back to supplicants.
units.literal: Original commentary: they hold guest protocol, receiving business, and submitting memorials and answering inquiries.

units.zh: 将、大夫以下之丧，掌使吊。
units.en: They carry the court’s condolences to the funerals of generals and officials of lower rank.
units.literal: For mourning of generals and grandees downward, they are dispatched to offer condolence.

units.zh: 本员七十人，中兴但三十人。
units.en: Western Han filled seventy slots; the restored court cut the corps to thirty.
units.literal: Originally the quota was seventy persons; at restoration only thirty.

units.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「汉皆用孝廉年五十，威容严恪能宾者为之。
units.en: Xun Chuo's Jin commentary on the offices says: "Han chose fifty-year-old filial and incorrupt men of grave bearing to serve as receptionists.
units.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "Han always appointed filial and incorrupt men aged fifty, of stern bearing and dignified manner able to receive guests.

units.zh: 明帝诏曰：『谒者乃尧之尊官，所以试舜宾于四门，四门穆穆者也。』
units.en: Emperor Ming called the post one of Yao's great offices, the office that tested Shun at the four gates.
units.literal: Emperor Ming's edict said: 'Receptionists were Yao's honored office, by which Shun was tested as guest at the four gates, and the four gates were reverent.

units.zh: 昔燕太子使荆轲劫始皇，变起两楹之间，其后谒者持匕首刺腋，高祖偃武行文，故易之以板。」
units.en: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward receptionists carried daggers at the armpit. Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced them with tablets."
units.literal: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward a receptionist stabbed him in the armpit with a dagger. Emperor Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced daggers with tablets."

units.zh: 初为灌谒者，满岁为给事谒者。
units.en: A novice begins as a bathed receptionist and after one year graduates to serving receptionist.
units.literal: At first they are bathed receptionists; when a full year is complete they become serving receptionists.

units.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「出府丞、长史、陵令，皆选仪容端正，任奉使者。」
units.en: Cai Zhi required handsome, dignified men for assistants, chief clerks, and mausoleum directors sent out as envoys."
units.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "For outgoing bureau assistants, chief clerks, and mausoleum directors, all are chosen for proper bearing and appearance, appointed as envoys on mission."

units.zh: 右属光禄勋。
units.en: The offices at right fall under the Minister of the Household.
units.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of the Household.

units.zh: 本注曰：职属光禄者，自五官将至羽林右监，凡七署。
units.en: Household-line commands run from the captain of the five bureaus through the right Feathered Forest superintendent—seven bureaus in all.
units.literal: Original commentary: offices subordinate to the Household, from the leader of gentlemen for the five offices down to the right superintendent of the Feathered Forest, in all seven bureaus.

units.zh: 自奉车都尉至谒者，以文属焉。
units.en: From chariot commandants through receptionists they count as civil adjuncts of the same ministry.
units.literal: From commandant of the imperial chariot down to receptionists, by civil subordination they attach there.

units.zh: 旧有左右曹，秩以二千石，上殿中，主受尚书奏事，平省之。
units.en: Western Han also posted left and right palace secretaries at two thousand bushels to take memorials from the Masters of Writing for screening inside the hall.
units.literal: Formerly there were left and right Cao at two-thousand-bushel rank, ascending to the hall, receiving Masters of Writing memorials and leveling and reviewing them.

units.zh: 世祖省，使小黄门郎受事，车驾出，给黄门郎兼。
units.en: Guangwu abolished those posts and had petty Yellow Gate gentlemen handle intake; on imperial progresses those same gentlemen double as escort.
units.literal: The Founding Ancestor eliminated them, having petty gentlemen of the Yellow Gate receive business; when the chariot goes out, petty gentlemen of the Yellow Gate double in the duty.

units.zh: 有请室令，车驾出，在前请所幸，徼车迎白，示重慎。
units.en: A director of the petition chamber once rode ahead to learn the emperor’s intended route so patrol cars could announce it—an emblem of care.
units.literal: There was a director of the petition chamber; when the chariot went out, he went ahead to request the intended destination, patrol chariots met him with the report, showing gravity and caution.

units.zh: 中兴但以郎兼，事讫罢，又省车、户、骑凡三将，如淳曰：「主车曰车郎，主户卫曰户郎。」
units.en: After the restoration gentlemen temporarily doubled these posts and were dismissed when duty ended; the chariot, household, and cavalry commanders were cut. Ru Chun glossed chariot gentlemen and household gentlemen."
units.literal: At restoration only gentlemen doubled the posts, dismissed when the affair ended; also eliminated were the three generals of chariots, household guard, and cavalry. Ru Chun said: "Those mastering chariots were called chariot gentlemen; those mastering household guard were called household gentlemen."

units.zh: 及羽林令。
units.en: The Feathered Forest director remained.
units.literal: Also the Director of Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 卫尉，卿一人，中二千石。
units.en: The Minister of the Guard: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
units.literal: Minister of the Guard, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌宫门卫士，宫中徼循事。
units.en: He commands the gate guards and palace patrols.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds palace-gate guardsmen and patrol affairs within the palace.

units.zh: 丞一人，比千石。
units.en: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 公车司马令一人，六百石。
units.en: One director of the public carriage gate and horse marshal at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of the public-carriage and horse marshal, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌宫南阙门，凡吏民上章，四方贡献，及征诣公车者。
units.en: He controls the palace’s southern portal for memorials, tribute convoys, and men summoned to the “public carriage” audience.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds the southern gate tower of the palace; all officials and commoners submitting memorials, regional tribute, and those summoned to the public carriage.

units.zh: 丞、尉各一人。
units.en: He has one assistant and one commandant.
units.literal: One assistant and one commandant each.

units.zh: 本注曰：丞选晓讳，掌知非法。
units.en: The assistant must know imperial taboos and flag irregular petitions.
units.literal: Original commentary: the assistant is chosen for knowledge of taboo names and masters knowing what is unlawful.

units.zh: 尉主阙门兵禁，戒非常。
units.en: The commandant enforces armed watch at the tower and bars emergencies.
units.literal: The commandant masters gate-tower troops and prohibitions, guarding against the extraordinary.

units.zh: 南宫卫士令一人，六百石。
units.en: One director of Southern Palace guards at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of Southern Palace guardsmen, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌南宫卫士。
units.en: He commands the Southern Palace guard detail.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds Southern Palace guardsmen.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 北宫卫士令一人，六百石。
units.en: One director of Northern Palace guards at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of Northern Palace guardsmen, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌北宫卫士。
units.en: He commands the Northern Palace guard detail.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds Northern Palace guardsmen.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 左右都候各一人，六百石。
units.en: Left and right metropolitan patrol commanders at six hundred bushels each.
units.literal: Left and right metropolitan patrol commanders, one each, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主剑戟士，徼循宫及天子有所收考。
units.en: They lead halberd guards on palace rounds and make arrests when the throne orders an inquiry.
units.literal: Original commentary: they command halberdiers, patrol the palace, and when the Son of Heaven has someone to seize or interrogate.

units.zh: 丞各一人。
units.en: Each command has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant each.

units.zh: 宫掖门，每门司马一人，比千石。
units.en: Every inner gate posts one major at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: For palace and harem gates, each gate has one major, comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：南宫南屯司马，主平城门；
units.en: The Southern Palace’s south camp major holds Pingcheng Gate;
units.literal: Original commentary: South Regiment Major of the Southern Palace masters Pingcheng Gate;

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏九人，卫士百二人。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists nine clerks and 102 guards."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Nine staff and one hundred two guards."

units.zh: 古今注曰建武十三年九月，初开此门。
units.en: Notes Ancient and Modern dates the gate's first opening to the ninth month of Jianwu 13.
units.literal: Notes Ancient and Modern says: in the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu, this gate was first opened.

units.zh: 宫门苍龙司马，主东门；
units.en: The Azure Dragon palace gate commandant holds the east gate;
units.literal: Palace Gate Azure Dragon Commandant masters the east gate;

units.zh: 案雒阳宫门名为苍龙阙门。
units.en: Luoyang's east palace gate was called the Azure Dragon Tower Gate.
units.literal: On investigation the Luoyang palace gate is named Azure Dragon Tower Gate.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏六人，卫士四十人。」
units.en: The Offices of Han gives the post six clerks and forty guards."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Six staff and forty guards."

units.zh: 玄武司马，主玄武门；
units.en: the Black Tortoise major holds Black Tortoise Gate;
units.literal: Black Tortoise Major masters Black Tortoise Gate;

units.zh: 北屯司马，主北门；
units.en: the north camp major holds the north gate;
units.literal: North Regiment Major masters the north gate;

units.zh: 北宫朱爵司马，主南掖门；
units.en: the Northern Palace’s Vermilion Sparrow major holds the south harem portal;
units.literal: Vermilion Sparrow Major of the Northern Palace masters the south harem gate;

units.zh: 东明司马，主东门；
units.en: the Dawn-clarity major holds the east inner gate;
units.literal: Dawn-clarity Major masters the east gate;

units.zh: 朔平司马，主北门：凡七门。
units.en: and the Pacified-north major holds the north inner gate—seven gates in all.
units.literal: Pacified-north Major masters the north gate: in all seven gates.

units.zh: 凡居宫中者，皆有口籍于门之所属。
units.en: Everyone quartered inside carries a mouth tally filed with the gate that controls his passage.
units.literal: All who dwell within the palace have mouth tallies registered with the gate to which they belong.

units.zh: 宫名两字，为铁印文符，案省符乃内之。
units.en: Each two-character gate name is cast on an iron tally; the seal must match before entry is granted.
units.literal: The palace name of two characters is an iron-seal text tally; they inspect the tally and only then admit them.

units.zh: 胡广曰：「符用木，长尺二寸，铁印以符之。」
units.en: Hu Guang noted that the wooden tally was one foot two inches long and authenticated by an iron seal."
units.literal: Hu Guang said: "The tally is of wood, one foot two inches long; an iron seal authenticates the tally."

units.zh: 若外人以事当入，本官长史为封棨传；
units.en: Official visitors must carry a wooden tally pass sealed by their agency's chief clerk;
units.literal: If an outsider must enter on business, the chief clerk of his home office seals a tally pass;

units.zh: 其有官位，出入令御者言其官。
units.en: Ranked officials declare their title to the coachman when passing in or out.
units.literal: If they have official rank, going out and in they order the charioteer to announce their office.

units.zh: 右属卫尉。
units.en: The offices at right belong to the Minister of the Guard.
units.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of the Guard.

units.zh: 本注曰：中兴省旅贲令，卫士一人丞。
units.en: The restoration abolished the Director of Rapid Escort and left each guard bureau with a single assistant.
units.literal: Original commentary: at restoration the Director of Rapid Escort was eliminated; the guard office has one assistant.

units.zh: 汉官目录曰：「右三卿，太尉所部。」
units.en: The Han Offices Catalogue places the three ministries at right under the Grand Commandant."
units.literal: The Han Offices Catalogue says: "The three ministers at right belong to the Grand Commandant."

units.zh: 太仆，卿一人，中二千石。
units.en: The Minister Coachman: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
units.literal: Minister Coachman, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌车马。
units.en: He is steward of the imperial stables and carriages.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds chariots and horses.

units.zh: 天子每出，奏驾上卤簿，用大驾则执御。
units.en: Whenever the emperor travels he arranges the chariot train and, for the grand progress, takes the reins himself.
units.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven goes out, he presents the chariot and ascends the guard of honor; when the grand chariot is used then he holds the reins.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏七十人，其七人四科，一人二百石，文学八人百石，六人斗食，七人佐，六人骑吏，三人假佐，三十一人学事，一人官医。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists seventy staff: seven graded officers, one at two hundred bushels, eight literary clerks, six dou-food clerks, seven assistants, six cavalry clerks, three acting assistants, thirty-one student clerks, and one court physician."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Seventy staff: seven in four grades, one at two hundred bushels, eight literary officers at one hundred bushels, six at dou-food rank, seven assistants, six cavalry clerks, three acting assistants, thirty-one student clerks, one court physician."

units.zh: 丞一人，比千石。
units.en: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 考工令一人，六百石。
units.en: One director of the imperial workshop at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of the workshop, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主作兵器弓弩刀铠之属，成则传执金吾入武库，及主织绶诸杂工。
units.en: He manufactured arms and armor, delivered finished goods to the metropolitan guard for the armory, and oversaw ribbon weaving and other crafts.
units.literal: Original commentary: he masters making weapons, crossbows, blades, armor, and the like; when finished they are passed to the Commandant of the Metropolitan Guard for entry into the armory, and he also masters weaving ribbons and various crafts.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏百九人。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists 109 clerks."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "One hundred nine staff."

units.zh: 左右丞各一人。
units.en: He has left and right assistants.
units.literal: Left and right assistants, one each.

units.zh: 车府令一人，六百石。
units.en: One director of the chariot depot at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of the chariot office, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主乘舆诸车。
units.en: He maintains every vehicle in the imperial garage.
units.literal: Original commentary: he masters all chariots of the imperial equipage.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 未央厩令一人，六百石。
units.en: One director of the Weiyang stable at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Director of the Weiyang stable, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：主乘舆及厩中诸马。
units.en: He tends the emperor's carriage horses and the rest of the Weiyang herd.
units.literal: Original commentary: he masters the imperial equipage and all horses in the stable.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏七十人，卒驺二十人。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists seventy clerks and twenty mounted runners."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Seventy staff and twenty mounted runners."

units.zh: 长乐厩丞一人。
units.en: One assistant director serves the Changle Palace stable.
units.literal: Assistant director of the Changle stable, one person.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏十五人，率驺二十人。
units.en: The Offices of Han says: "Fifteen clerks and twenty mounted runners,
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Fifteen staff and twenty mounted runners.

units.zh: 苜蓿苑官田所一人守之。」
units.en: and one warden for the alfalfa park fields."
units.literal: One man guards the alfalfa park official fields."

units.zh: 右属太仆。
units.en: The offices at right report to the Minister Coachman.
units.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister Coachman.

units.zh: 本注曰：旧有六厩，皆六百石令，前书曰，有大厩、未央、家马三令，各五丞一尉。
units.en: Western Han ran six stables under six-hundred-bushel directors; the Former Book names great, Weiyang, and imperial horse stables, each with five deputies and a commandant.
units.literal: Original commentary: formerly there were six stables, each with a six-hundred-bushel director; the Former Book says there were directors of the great stable, Weiyang, and imperial horses—three directors, each with five assistants and one commandant.

units.zh: 又车府、路軨、骑马、骏马四令丞。
units.en: There were also directors for the chariot depot, road chariots, riding horses, and fine horses.
units.literal: Also the chariot office, road-chariot, riding horse, and fine horse—four directors and assistants.

units.zh: 晋灼曰：「六厩名也，主马万匹。」
units.en: Jin Zhuo explained that the six names denoted stables keeping as many as ten thousand horses.
units.literal: Jin Zhuo said: "These were the names of the six stables, mastering ten thousand horses."

units.zh: 中兴省约，但置一厩。
units.en: The restored court kept only one stable.
units.literal: At restoration they were reduced and only one stable was set.

units.zh: 后置左骏令、厩，别主乘舆御马，后或并省。
units.en: Later a separate left fine-horse stable was added for imperial carriage mounts, then sometimes abolished again.
units.literal: Later they set up a left fine-horse director and stable, separately mastering imperial carriage horses; later these too were sometimes merged and cut.

units.zh: 又有牧师范，皆令官，主养马，分在河西六郡界中，中兴皆省，唯汉阳有流马菀，但以羽林郎监领。
units.en: Pastoral officials once bred remounts across six western commanderies until the restoration abolished them; only Hanyang’s “flowing horse” breeding ground survived, overseen by a Feathered Forest officer.
units.literal: Moreover there were pastoral zones and stud farms, each with a director official, mastering horse breeding, distributed within the borders of the six western commanderies; at restoration all were eliminated; only Hanyang retained a “flowing horse” park, supervised solely by a Feathered Forest gentleman.

units.zh: 廷尉，卿一人，中二千石。
units.en: The Minister of Justice: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
units.literal: Minister of Justice, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌平狱，奏当所应。
units.en: He supervises criminal justice and memorializes the appropriate sentences.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds leveling of prisons and memorializing what judgments should be.

units.zh: 凡郡国谳疑罪，皆处当以报。
units.en: Doubtful cases from the provinces were decided and reported with recommended sentences.
units.literal: For doubtful crimes in commanderies and kingdoms, all are judged and reported with the appropriate sentence.

units.zh: 胡广曰：「谳，质也。」
units.en: Hu Guang glossed yan as "to verify."
units.literal: Hu Guang said: "Yan means to verify."

units.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏百四十人，其十一人四科，十六人二百石廷吏，文学十六人百石，十三人狱史，二十七人佐，二十六人骑吏，三十人假佐，一人官医。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists 140 staff including graded officers, court clerks, literary clerks, prison clerks, assistants, cavalry clerks, acting assistants, and one court physician."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "One hundred forty staff: eleven in four grades, sixteen two-hundred-bushel court clerks, sixteen literary officers at one hundred bushels, thirteen prison clerks, twenty-seven assistants, twenty-six cavalry clerks, thirty acting assistants, one court physician."

units.zh: 正、左监各一人。
units.en: The ministry staffs one rectifying judge and one left prison superintendent.
units.literal: One rectifying judge and one left superintendent each.

units.zh: 左平一人，六百石。
units.en: One left “leveling” officer at six hundred bushels.
units.literal: Left leveling officer, one person, six hundred bushels.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌平决诏狱。
units.en: He adjudicates cases held in the emperor’s special prisons.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds leveling judgments in edict prisons.

units.zh: 右属廷尉。
units.en: The offices at right fall under the Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 本注曰：孝武帝以下，置中都官狱二十六所，各令长名世祖中兴皆省，唯廷尉及雒阳有诏狱。
units.en: From Emperor Wu on the capital ran twenty-six separate prison bureaus, each with its own warden; Guangwu abolished them, leaving only the Minister of Justice’s jails and Luoyang’s imperial prison.
units.literal: Original commentary: from Emperor Xiaowu downward, twenty-six capital-office prisons were established, each with a director or chief by name; at the Founding Ancestor’s restoration all were eliminated; only the Minister of Justice and Luoyang retained edict prisons.

units.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「正月旦，石官朝贺，光禄勋刘嘉、廷尉赵世各辞不能朝，高赐举奏：『皆以被病笃困，空文武之位，阙上卿之赞，既无忠信断金之用，而有败礼伤化之尤，不谨不敬！
units.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies records: "On New Year's day Liu Jia and Zhao Shi pleaded illness and stayed away; Gao Ci impeached them for deserting their posts and harming court ritual, declaring them negligent and disrespectful:
units.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "On the first day of the first month, when stone officials attended court congratulations, Minister of the Household Liu Jia and Commandant of Justice Zhao Shi each pleaded illness and could not attend. Gao Ci memorialized and impeached them: 'Both claim grave illness, leaving civil and military posts empty and lacking the support of upper ministers; they are useless for loyal, faithful solidarity and are guilty of the grave fault of damaging ritual and harming custom—negligent and disrespectful!

units.zh: 请廷尉治嘉罪，河南尹治世罪。』
units.en: he asked that Jia be tried by the commandant of justice and Shi by the governor of Henan
units.literal: I ask that the Commandant of Justice try Jia's crime and the Governor of Henan try Shi's crime.

units.zh: 议以世掌廷尉，故转属他官。」
units.en: though Shi's own office required transferring the case."
units.literal: Because Shi headed the Commandant of Justice, the case was transferred to another office."

units.zh: 大鸿胪，卿一人，中二千石。
units.en: The Grand Herald: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
units.literal: Grand Herald, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 周礼「象胥」，干宝注曰今鸿胪。
units.en: The Zhou "image interpreters" were, in Gan Bao's gloss, the Grand Herald of later times.
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou "image interpreters"; Gan Bao's commentary says this is today's Grand Herald.

units.zh: 本注曰：掌诸侯及四方归义蛮夷。
units.en: He receives feudal princes and foreign peoples who have pledged allegiance.
units.literal: Original commentary: he holds feudal lords and barbarians of the four quarters who have submitted in righteousness.

units.zh: 其郊庙行礼，赞导，请行事，既可，以命群司。
units.en: At suburban and ancestral rites he prompts the liturgy, seeks permission to proceed, then instructs the ministries once the emperor assents.
units.literal: At suburban and temple rites he assists and leads, requests the carrying out of affairs; once approved, by this he orders the host of offices.

units.zh: 诸王入朝，当郊迎，典其礼仪。
units.en: When princes come to audience he meets them at the suburban station and directs their ceremonial approach.
units.literal: When kings enter court, he should meet them at the suburban altar and holds their ritual protocol.

units.zh: 及郡国上计，匡四方来，亦属焉。
units.en: Regional accounting missions and inspectors from abroad likewise report through his ministry.
units.literal: And when commanderies and kingdoms present annual accounts, and correctors from the four quarters arrive, these also attach to him.

units.zh: 皇子拜王，赞授印绶。
units.en: When a son of the throne is enfeoffed as a king, he presents the seal and sash on the emperor’s behalf.
units.literal: When imperial sons are invested as kings, he assists in presenting the seal and ribbons.

units.zh: 及拜诸侯、诸侯嗣子及四方夷狄封者，台下鸿胪召拜之。
units.en: Investitures of feudal lords, their heirs, and foreign rulers summoned for enfeoffment are conducted below the hall steps under the Grand Herald’s call.
units.literal: And when investing feudal lords, heirs of feudal lords, and those from the four quarters barbarians who are to be enfeoffed, below the terrace the Grand Herald summons them for the investiture.

units.zh: 王薨则使吊之，及拜王嗣。
units.en: On a king’s death he sends condolences; he also oversees the heir’s investiture.
units.literal: When a king dies he dispatches someone to offer condolences, and for investing the king’s successor.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 比千石。
units.en: That assistant ranks at one thousand bushels equivalent.
units.literal: Comparable to one thousand bushels.

units.zh: 大行令一人，六百石，本注曰：主诸郎。
units.en: One director of grand processions at six hundred bushels, in charge of the ministry’s gentlemen.
units.literal: Director of grand processions, one person, six hundred bushels; original commentary: he commands the various gentlemen.

units.zh: 丞一人。
units.en: He has one assistant.
units.literal: One assistant.

units.zh: 治礼郎四十七人。
units.en: Forty-seven rite-regulating gentlemen assist at state ceremonies.
units.literal: Rite-regulating gentlemen, forty-seven persons.

units.zh: 汉官曰：「其四人四科，五人二百石，文学五人百石，九人斗食，六人佐，六人学事，十二人守学事。」
units.en: The Offices of Han lists four graded officers, five at two hundred bushels, five literary clerks at one hundred, nine dou-food staff, six assistants, six student clerks, and twelve supervising student clerks."
units.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Four men in four grades, five at two hundred bushels, five literary officers at one hundred bushels, nine at dou-food rank, six assistants, six student clerks, twelve supervising student clerks."

units.zh: 东观书曰：「主斋祠傧赞九宾。
units.en: The Eastern Lodge Record says: "They manage fasting rites and guest protocol,
units.literal: The Eastern Lodge Record says: "They preside over fasting sacrifices, protocol, and assisting the nine guests.

units.zh: 又有公室，主调中都官斗食以下，功次相补。」
units.en: with a separate office ranking capital clerks below dou-food grade by merit."
units.literal: There is also a public office that coordinates capital officials at dou-food rank and below, filling posts by merit in order."

units.zh: 案卢植礼注曰：「大行郎亦如谒者，兼举形貌。」
units.en: Lu Zhi noted that grand procession gentlemen, like receptionists, also assessed appearance.
units.literal: Lu Zhi's Rites commentary says: "Grand procession gentlemen, like receptionists, also report on physical appearance."

units.zh: 右属大鸿胪。
units.en: The offices at right belong to the Grand Herald.
units.literal: Those on the right belong to the Grand Herald.

units.zh: 本注曰：承秦有典属国，别主四方夷狄朝贡侍子，成帝时省并大鸿胪。
units.en: Qin's office of dependent states once handled foreign tribute and hostage princes until Emperor Cheng folded it into the Grand Herald.
units.literal: Original commentary: inheriting Qin there was a director of dependent states, separately mastering the four quarters' barbarians' court tribute and hostage sons; in Emperor Cheng's time it was eliminated and merged into the Grand Herald.

units.zh: 中兴省驿官、别火二令、丞，如淳曰：「汉仪注：『别火，狱令官，主治改火事。』」
units.en: The restoration cut the relay and Separate Fire directorates. Ru Chun glossed Separate Fire as the prison office that managed the ritual change of hearth fires."
units.literal: At restoration the relay-office and separate-fire directors and assistants were eliminated. Ru Chun said: "The Han Ceremonies commentary: 'Separate Fire was a prison directorate, mastering the seasonal change of hearth fires.'"

units.zh: 及郡邸长、丞，但令郎治郡邸。
units.en: Commandery hostel chiefs and assistants were reduced so that gentlemen alone ran the hostels.
units.literal: As for commandery hostel chiefs and assistants, only gentlemen were ordered to manage commandery hostels.

units.zh: 汉官目录曰：「右三官，司徒所部。」
units.en: The Han Offices Catalogue lists the three offices at right under the Minister of Education."
units.literal: The Han Offices Catalogue says: "The three offices at right belong to the Minister of Education."

units.zh: 上曰：「吾聞李斯相秦皇帝，有善歸主，有惡自予。
units.en: The Sovereign said, “They say Li Si, as Qin’s chancellor, credited the throne with every success and himself with every failure;
units.literal: The Sovereign said, “I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor to the First Emperor of Qin, whatever was good he attributed to his lord; whatever was bad he took on himself.

units.zh: 五月，封舅曼子侍中騎都尉光祿大夫王莽為新都侯。
units.en: In the fifth month, maternal uncle Man's son Wang Mang, Attendant at the Palace and Cavalry Commandant Guanglu Grandee, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu.
units.literal: Fifth month, enfeoffed maternal uncle Man son Attendant at the Palace Cavalry Commandant Guanglu Grandee Wang Mang as Xindu Marquis.

units.zh: 年二十，遭王莽敗，世祖即位於冀州。
units.en: At twenty he lived through Wang Mang's fall and watched Liu Xiu raise the Han banner in Ji.
units.literal: At twenty he encountered Wang Mang's collapse, and the Founding Ancestor took the throne in Ji Province.

units.zh: 史臣曰：燕太子吐一言，田先生吞舌而死；
units.en: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word, and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;
units.literal: The historiographer says: The Crown Prince of Yan spoke one word and Master Tian swallowed his tongue and died;

units.zh: 建始以來，王氏始執國命，哀、平短祚，莽遂篡位，蓋其威福所由來者漸矣！
units.en: Since Jianshi, the Wang clan began to grasp the state's fate. Ai and Ping had short reigns, Mang then usurped the throne—indeed the source of his power and fortune was gradual!
units.literal: Jianshi since, Wang clan began grasped state fate, Ai, Ping short blessings, Mang then usurped position, cover his power blessing what from came gradually indeed!

units.zh: 晉世王導爲司徒，右長史干寶撰立官府，《職儀》已具。
units.en: Under Jin, Wang Dao was Minister of Education; his right senior recorder Gan Bao drew up the office establishment—the Protocols of Office already cover it.
units.literal: In Jin times Wang Dao served as Minister of Education; right senior recorder Gan Bao compiled the establishment of the government office—the "Protocols of Office" are complete.

units.zh: 《巴渝》，漢高帝命工人作也；
units.en: "Bayu," commissioned by Han Gaozu from his artisans;
units.literal: "Bayu" was made when Emperor Gaozu of Han ordered craftsmen to compose it;

units.zh: 及論功當封，太尉胡廣時錄尚書事，承旨奏黜撫，天下怨之。
units.en: When honors were due for his victories, Grand Commandant Hu Guang—then directing the Secretariat—carried out an order to strip Teng Fu of recognition, and public opinion turned bitterly against the court.
units.literal: When merit was discussed and he ought to have been enfeoffed, Grand Commandant Hu Guang at the time held the office of recording imperial secretary affairs; receiving intent he memorialized to dismiss Fu—the realm resented it.

units.zh: 是以尧称则天，不屈颍阳之高；
units.en: So Yao could mirror Heaven and still leave the recluses of Yingyang untroubled in their height;
units.literal: Therefore Yao was said to pattern himself on Heaven, yet he did not bend the height of those at Yingyang;

units.zh: 博士范升奏毁党曰：“臣闻尧不须许由、巢父，而建号天下；
units.en: Erudite Fan Sheng attacked him: "Yao needed neither Xu You nor Chao Father to rule the world;
units.literal: Erudite Fan Sheng memorialized to attack Dang, saying, "Your servant has heard that Yao did not need Xu You and Chao Fu yet established his title over the realm;

units.zh: 光又眠不应，良久，乃张目熟视，曰：“昔唐尧著德，巢父洗耳。
units.en: Yan kept his eyes shut, then opened them slowly: "When Yao shone with virtue, Chao Father still washed the taint from his ears.
units.literal: Guang again slept and did not answer; after a long while he then opened his eyes, stared fixedly, and said, "In antiquity Tang Yao displayed virtue, yet Chao Father washed his ears.

units.zh: 孝章皇帝深惟古人之道，助三正之微，定律著令，冀承天心，順物性命，以致時雍。
units.en: Emperor Zhang pondered antiquity, harmonized the three beginnings in law, and hoped to align Heaven with the nature of things for universal peace.
units.literal: Emperor Zhang deeply pondered the Way of ancients, assisting the subtlety of the three beginnings; fixing statutes and establishing orders; hoping to inherit Heaven's heart, comply with creatures' natures and lives, so as to bring seasonal harmony.

units.zh: 肅宗集諸儒於白虎觀，恭特以經明得召，與其議。
units.en: When Emperor Zhang convened scholars at White Tiger Hall, Gong was invited on strength of his classical expertise and joined the debates.
units.literal: Emperor Suzong assembled the Confucians at White Tiger Hall; Gong was specially summoned because of his clarity on the classics and participated in their discussions.

units.zh: 初，肅宗時，斷獄皆以冬至之前，自後論者互多駁異。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhang capital cases had to conclude before the winter solstice; later scholars quarreled endlessly over the rule.
units.literal: Formerly, in Emperor Suzong's time, cutting prison cases was all before the winter solstice; afterward debaters mutually increased refutations and differences.

units.zh: 建初元年，肅宗詔舉賢良方正，大司農劉寬舉丕。
units.en: In Jianchu 1 Emperor Zhang sought worthy candidates; Minister of Agriculture Liu Kuan nominated Lu Pi.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianchu, Emperor Suzong ordered recommendation of worthy and upright men; Minister of Agriculture Liu Kuan recommended Pi.

units.zh: 其後帝巡狩之趙，特被引見，難問經傳，厚加賞賜。
units.en: Later, when the emperor toured Zhao, Pi was specially summoned, examined on the classics, and richly rewarded.
units.literal: Afterward, when the emperor toured Zhao, Pi was specially summoned for audience, questioned on the classics, and richly rewarded.

units.zh: 武帝時，生有罪免，國除。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu, Sheng was removed for a crime and the fief was abolished.
units.literal: During Emperor Wu's reign, Sheng was removed for crime, and the state was abolished.

units.zh: 武帝末年，悔征伐之事，乃封丞相為富民侯。
units.en: Late in Emperor Wu's reign, he regretted the campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.
units.literal: At Emperor Wu's late years, he regretted campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.

units.zh: 長老皆言武帝時縣官嘗自漁，海魚不出，後復予民，魚乃出。
units.en: Elders all say that in Emperor Wu's time, when the county offices themselves fished, sea fish did not appear; later, when fishing was returned to the people, the fish then appeared.
units.literal: Elders all say that in Emperor Wu's time when county offices fished themselves, sea fish did not emerge; later returned to people, fish then emerged.

units.zh: 董仲舒說上曰：「春秋它穀不書，至於麥禾不成則書之，以此見聖人於五穀最重麥與禾也。
units.en: Dong Zhongshu said to the emperor, 'In the Spring and Autumn Annals other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail to ripen it is recorded—showing that the sage gave greatest weight among the five grains to wheat and millet.
units.literal: Dong Zhongshu advised the emperor: 'In Spring and Autumn, other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail it is recorded-showing sages gave greatest weight among grains to wheat and millet.

units.zh: 願陛下幸詔大司農，使關中民益種宿麥，令毋後時。」
units.en: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture to have the people of Guanzhong plant more winter wheat and not miss the season.'
units.literal: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture that Guanzhong people increase winter wheat and not miss seasonal timing.'

units.zh: 下詔曰：「
units.en: He issued edict: "
units.literal: He issued edict: "

units.zh: 方今之務，在於力農。」
units.en: The foremost task now is to strengthen agriculture."
units.literal: At present the main task lies in strengthening agriculture."

units.zh: 以趙過為搜粟都尉。
units.en: He appointed Zhao Guo as Commandant for Grain Collection.
units.literal: He made Zhao Guo Commandant for Grain Collection.

units.zh: 幼有志節，慕荊軻、聶政為人，年三十始折節讀書。
units.en: In youth he had resolve and integrity, admired Jing Ke and Nie Zheng, and only at thirty began to restrain himself and study books.
units.literal: In youth he had resolve and integrity, admired the conduct of Jing Ke and Nie Zheng, and only at thirty began to restrain himself and study books.

units.zh: 以郡國選詣博士，受業孔安國。
units.en: Recommended by his commandery, he entered the academy and studied with Kong Anguo.
units.literal: Selected by his commandery and kingdom he went to the erudite and received instruction from Kong Anguo.

units.zh: 元鼎中，征式代石慶為御史大夫。
units.en: In Yuanding the court called Bu Shi to replace Shi Qing as imperial counselor.
units.literal: In the Yuanding period he summoned Shi to replace Shi Qing as imperial counselor.

units.zh: 以山東無兄問者，乃西入關，因涿郡盧植，事扶風馬融。
units.en: Finding no teacher of stature east of the mountains, he crossed into the west and, introduced by Lu Zhi of Zhu, studied under Ma Rong of Fufeng.
units.literal: Because east of the mountains there was no one he could consult, he went west through the passes, and through Lu Zhi of Zhuo commandery served Ma Rong of Fufeng.

units.zh: 臣朔年二十二，長九尺三寸，目若懸珠，齒若編貝，勇若孟賁，捷若慶忌，廉若鮑叔，信若尾生。
units.en: I am twenty-two, stand nine feet three inches, my eyes shine like pearls and my teeth line up like shells; in courage I match Meng Ben, in agility Qingji, in integrity Bao Shu, in good faith Weisheng.
units.literal: Your servant Shuo is twenty-two years old, nine feet three inches tall, with eyes like suspended pearls and teeth like strung shells, brave as Meng Ben, swift as Qingji, incorrupt as Bao Shu, trustworthy as Weisheng.

units.zh: 覽考工記、大戴禮盛德篇，以明堂之制不同，遂著明堂制度論曰：
units.en: Reading the Records of the Craftsman and the "Accomplished Virtue" chapter of Elder Dai's Rites, and finding the Mingtang regulations at odds, he wrote an essay On the Mingtang System, which says:
units.literal: Reading the Records of the Craftsman and the "Accomplished Virtue" chapter of the Elder Dai's Rites, and finding the Mingtang regulations differ, he therefore wrote an essay On the Mingtang System, saying:

units.zh: 言九室者，則案大戴盛德之篇以為源，是伯喈之倫所持。
units.en: the nine-chamber school takes Elder Dai's "Accomplished Virtue" chapter as its source—the party of Cai Yong.
units.literal: those who speak of nine chambers take the "Accomplished Virtue" chapter of Elder Dai as source—this is what the party of Cai Yong holds.

units.zh: 然竊以為戴氏聞三十六戶、七十二牖，弗見其制，靡知所置，便謂一室有四戶之窗，計其戶牖之數，即以為九室耳。
units.en: Yet I think the Dai clan heard of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows, never saw the actual plan, and simply assumed four doors and windows per chamber—counting doors and windows, they called it nine chambers.
units.literal: Yet I privately think that the Dai clan heard of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows, did not see the regulation, and did not know where to place them, and therefore supposed one chamber had four doors and windows; calculating the number of doors and windows, they took it to be nine chambers.

units.zh: 孝宣承統，纂修洪業，亦講論六藝，招選茂異，而蕭望之、梁丘賀、夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖，尹更始以儒術進，劉向，王褒以文章顯，將相則張安世、趙充國、魏相、丙吉、於定國、杜延年，治民則黃霸、王成、龔遂、鄭弘、召信臣、韓延壽、尹翁歸、趙廣漢、嚴延年、張敞之屬，皆有功跡見述於世。
units.en: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too expounded the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men. Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction for their writing; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; and among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All left achievements celebrated in their age.
units.literal: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too discussed the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men: Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction through literary composition; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All had achievements recounted in their age.

units.zh: 商公武、武兄無故，皆以宣帝舅封。
units.en: Wang Shang's father was Wang Wu, and Wu's elder brother Wang Wugu; both received marquisates as maternal uncles of Emperor Xuan.
units.literal: Shang's father was Wu; Wu's elder brother was Wugu; both were enfeoffed because they were uncles on the mother's side of Emperor Xuan.

units.zh: 皇考者，孝宣帝父也。
units.en: The Lamented Imperial Father was Emperor Xuan's father.
units.literal: The Imperial Father was the father of Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety.

units.zh: 帝崩，太子襲尊號，是爲孝元帝。
units.en: When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded as Emperor Yuan.
units.literal: The emperor died; the heir apparent assumed the exalted title—this was Emperor Yuan of Filial Piety.

units.zh: 哀王者，帝之少弟，與太子遊學相長大。
units.en: Prince Ai was the emperor's younger brother; he and the crown prince had studied and grown up together.
units.literal: Prince Ai was the emperor's younger brother; he and the heir apparent studied and traveled together and grew up together.

units.zh: 宣帝微時依倚史氏。
units.en: In his lowly days Emperor Xuan relied on the Shi family.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan was in humble circumstances he relied on the Shi clan.

units.zh: 及宣帝即尊位，恭已死，三子，高、曾、玄。
units.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Gong was already dead, leaving three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan assumed the exalted throne, Gong was already dead; he had three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.

units.zh: 宣帝疾病，拜高爲大司馬、車騎將軍，領尚書事。
units.en: When Emperor Xuan fell ill, he appointed Shi Gao Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry with oversight of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan was ill, Gao was appointed Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry, overseeing Masters of Writing affairs.

units.zh: 且皇后謹慎，先帝又愛太子，吾豈可違指！
units.en: Besides, the empress is prudent, and the late emperor loved the crown prince. How could I go against his intent!
units.literal: Moreover the empress is careful and cautious; the former emperor also loved the heir apparent—how could I go against his intent!

units.zh: 贊曰：自宜、元、成、哀外戚興者，許、史、三王、丁、傅之家，皆重侯累將，窮貴極富，見其位矣，未見其人也。
units.en: The historian's judgment: From the reigns of Xuan through Ai, the consort clans—the Xu, the Shi, the three Wang lines, the Ding, and the Fu—stacked marquisates and generalships until they towered in wealth and rank; you could see their offices, rarely the men who deserved them.
units.literal: The appraiser says: From Emperor Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai, those by whom outer kin rose—the houses of Xu, Shi, the three Wangs, Ding, and Fu—all piled marquisates and repeated generalships, exhausted nobility and exhausted wealth; one sees their positions, one has not seen their persons.

units.zh: 成帝時，天下亡兵革之事，號為安樂，然俗奢侈，不以畜聚為意。
units.en: Under Cheng there was peace but high-consumption culture and weak saving behavior.
units.literal: In Chengdi's time the realm had no war affairs and was called peaceful and joyful, yet customs were extravagant and did not intend accumulation.

units.zh: 永始二年，梁國、平原郡比年傷水災，人相食，刺史守相坐免。
units.en: Repeated flood famine caused cannibalism and administrative dismissals.
units.literal: In Yongshi year two, Liang state and Pingyuan commandery had repeated flood damage; people ate one another; inspectors, governors, and commandery heads were removed for culpability.
